purpose: Discover a previously unconnected monitoring station, archive actual observations and attest reproducibility on a local blockchain; not physical truth or ecological improvement.
selectionRule: Sort eligible catalog entries by station ID and then series ID; choose the first with matching station metadata and at least two approved unqualified observations in the frozen window.
successCriteria: A station ID absent from alreadyConnectedStationIds is selected from archived catalog responses without hardcoding the selected ID.
Raw response hashes, selection, normalization and evidence commitment can be reproduced offline.
The existing evidence registry accepts the honest commitment with three of four registered local test identities and one unavailable identity.
Altered raw data or metadata fail verification against the original external commitment.
Two compromised identities cannot reach quorum; duplicated and unauthorized attestations fail.
A false but internally consistent upstream snapshot and three colluding authorized identities are demonstrated as residual vulnerabilities, not claimed to be detected.
trustAssumptions: The initial catalog origin, territory and rules are configured once by an operator; new station IDs are discovered automatically within this provider.
HTTPS binds acquisition to the publisher endpoint. USGS responses are not sensor-signed, and collector signatures would not become USGS signatures.
All local test identities share one test host and are not independent real operators.
Publisher approval is preserved as a publisher claim, not independent field validation.
Cryptographic commitments protect a retained snapshot; they cannot prove calibration, physical truth, undisclosed omissions or honest initial publication.
